figures.finding: Where salary is more than 75% of taxable income, tax for the year from 1 July 2026 is nil to Rs 600,000, then 1%, 11%, 20%, 25%, 29%, 32% and 35% above Rs 7,000,000 (as substituted by the Finance Act, 2026); other individuals pay 15% to 45% above Rs 600,000 with a 10% surcharge above Rs 10 million.
figures.applies: Individuals, tax year 2027 (1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027)

The following tax rates are applicable in other cases (for non-salaried individuals and AOPs): Taxable income (PKR) Tax on column 1 (PKR) Tax on excess (%) Over (column 1) Not over 0 600,000 0 600,000 1,200,000 15 1,200,000 1,600,000 90,000 20 1,600,000 3,200,000 170,000 30 3,200,000 5,600,000 650,000 40 5,600,000 1,610,000 45 Non-salaried individuals and AOPs with taxable income exceeding PKR 10 million in a year must pay a surcharge equal to 10% of their income tax.

figures.finding: Social security and Employees' Old-Age Benefits contributions are nominal, collected mainly from employers, with a nominal employee share to EOBI.

sources.said: Nominal social security and Employees Old Age Benefit contribution is collected from the employers. Employee is also responsible for a nominal contribution in respect of Employees Old Age Benefit. Employers are responsible to collect and pay on a monthly basis.

figures.finding: The whole tax on salary is deducted at source at the salaried rates; payments for services to individuals bear withholding at rates that depend on whether the vendor is an active taxpayer.

value.kind: employer deduction on the salaried table

sources.said: In general, the entire tax is deducted at source on payment of salary to individuals at rates mentioned above for salaried individuals. Varying WHT rates are prescribed for different goods, services, and contracts provided and executed by individuals and AOPs, based on status of the vendor being an active taxpayer or not.

figures.finding: Remuneration of a non-resident entertainer paid by a resident is Pakistan-source income; a payment to a non-resident not otherwise covered bears 20% deducted from the gross, and royalties 15%.

sources.said: Where the business of a non-resident person comprises the rendering of independent services (including professional services and the services of entertainers and sports persons), the Pakistan-source business income of the person shall include [in addition to any amounts treated as Pakistan-source income under sub-section (3)] any remuneration derived by the person where the remuneration is paid by a resident person or borne by a permanent establishment in Pakistan of a non-resident person.]

(2) Subject to sub-section (3), every person paying an amount to a non-resident person (other than an amount to which sub-section (1) 3[or sub- section (1A) 4[, (1AA)] 5[, (1AAA), 6[(1C)] or (2A)] applies)] shall deduct tax from the gross amount paid at the rate specified in Division II of Part III of the First Schedule.
(2) The rate of tax to be deducted under sub-section (2) of section 152 shall be 5[20]% of the gross amount paid.]
The rate of tax imposed under section 6 on payments to non-residents shall be 15% of the gross amount of the royalty or fee for technical services

figures.finding: An author whose literary or artistic work took more than 24 months may spread a lump-sum royalty equally over that year and the two before.
figures.applies: Authors of literary or artistic works

sources.said: 89. Authors. — Where the time taken by an author of a literary or artistic work to complete the work exceeds twenty-four months, the author may elect to treat any lump sum amount received by the author in a tax year on account of royalties in respect of the work as having been received in that tax year and the preceding two tax years in equal proportions.

figures.finding: Federal sales tax of 18% falls on goods; services are taxed by the provinces.

sources.said: VAT (locally termed as ‘sales tax’) is ordinarily levied at 18% on the value of goods, unless specifically exempt, alter allowing related input credits. Provinces levy sales tax on certain services.

figures.finding: The tax year runs from 1 July to 30 June, and an individual's return is due by 30 September after the year ends.

sources.said: The tax year is 1 July through 30 June.

figures.finding: The 20% deducted under s. 152(2) from a payment to a non-resident is not a final tax: s. 169 makes final only the deductions it lists (s. 152(1E), s. 152A and others), not s. 152(2), and s. 152(2) is not declared a minimum tax, so the non-resident's income stays chargeable on assessment with the deduction taken into account; s. 152(2) does not apply where the amount is taxable to a Pakistan permanent establishment with the Commissioner's approval, paid through a representative, or not chargeable.

exclusions: taxable to a PE with approval

figures.applies: Payments to non-residents not covered by other sub-sections of s. 152 (Income Tax Ordinance 2001 as amended to the Finance Act 2026)

sources.said: 169. Tax collected or deducted as a final tax.— (1) This section shall apply … (b) the 2[tax required to be deducted] is a final tax under 3[sub- section (1E) of section 152, 152A] … (2) Where this section applies — (a) the income shall not be chargeable to tax under any head of income in computing the taxable income of the person; … (3) Sub-section (2) does not apply to an amount — … (b) with the written approval of the Commissioner, that is taxable to a permanent establishment in Pakistan of the non-resident person;

figures.finding: Sindh's sales tax on services is 15%; the services of performing and other artists are exempt (not stage, set, lighting or costume designers'), and a provider whose annual turnover is at most Rs 4 million is exempt unless serving a withholding agent or a registered person.
figures.applies: Sindh, as consolidated to the Sindh Finance Act 2026, read 2026-11-03; the other provinces and the capital were not read, and the game holds no province for a person, so no province's rate is applied.

sources.said: sales tax on the provision of a taxable service at the rate of fifteen per cent of value of the taxable service
Services of performing and other artists: exempt; the exemption shall not be applicable to services provided or rendered by stage designers, set designers, lighting designers and costume designers

figures.finding: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's sales tax on services is 15%; performing artists' services, authors' and composers' original works included, are exempt where they reflect cultural and societal values for the public at large, but live concerts, stage shows, dramas and like commercial entertainment stay taxable, and no turnover threshold is set in the Act (the Policy Board may notify one). Balochistan's is 15% on every service not in its First Schedule of exemptions, from 1 July 2025.

KP.performingArtists: exempt where cultural and for the public at large; commercial entertainment (live concerts, stage shows, dramas) taxable

Balochistan.basis: every service not in the First Schedule

figures.applies: KP's Act as updated to its Finance Act 2026 and Balochistan's Finance Act 2025, read 2026-11-03 (Balochistan's section 10 checked against the scan's page image). The game holds no province for a person, so no province's rate is applied.
